verdict.rationale: Name.com documents a first-party MCP server that lets AI agents such as Cursor and Claude Desktop call Core API operations on the user's behalf. It also publishes an agent skill file covering domain-settings management. Together these let a user drive the product with natural-language commands, but only through a third-party AI client, not a native natural-language interface. Missing for 10: a built-in natural-language interface in the product itself, documentation of which operations work reliably via natural-language prompts, and independent or hands-on corroboration of natural-language operation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: The name.com Model Context Protocol (MCP) server lets AI agents (e.g., Cursor, Claude Desktop) safely call name.com Core API operations on your behalf.
manage domain settings (locks, privacy, autorenew, contacts)
